title: Hooghoudt/Ernst IPOS 1..5 Domain Readiness Evidence
material_findings: Legacy input admissibility is broader than mathematical evaluator admissibility and cannot be copied as the modern validity contract.
IPOS 1 is the smallest separately implementable Hooghoudt response family.
IPOS 2 and 3 share an equivalent-depth helper whose x=0.5 formula-family transition is not exactly continuous and must remain explicit in branch metadata.
IPOS 4 and 5 require stricter positive-divisor and logarithm-domain checks than the legacy reader enforces.
IPOS 4 has a hydraulic-response kink at gwl=zintf when kvtop differs from kvbot.
IPOS 5 does not use kvbot and a normalized IPOS5 parameter object should not retain that unused legacy field.
The legacy diffl=1e-10 activation cutoff remains a compatibility/branch-policy issue and is not normalized by this parent workunit.
